review_scope: Complete FedRAMP40-line and residency85-line articles and five complete compliance reusables read. All75 candidates plus non-candidate context, independent region/certification scopes, client compatibility, pricing and32 listed model occurrences retained. No current certification, legal clearance, credentials, costs or native change.

claims.statement: FedRAMP guidance declares Copilot cloud/data-residency product scope; metadata is not proof of account eligibility or certification.
The source permits a US data-residency enterprise to restrict plan users to models described as FedRAMP Moderate-certified; the geographic/account precondition is essential.
FedRAMP model availability is supplied by shared availability and US-model reusables; list membership is not independent certification or target observation.
Compatible clients, supported features and pricing changes are dependencies of enforcement, not optional omissions from applicability.
The Restrict Copilot to FedRAMP models policy is described as disabled by default, configured under enterprise Features and affecting request pricing; no change is applied here.
Enterprise policy navigation is separately reviewed context, not current permission or an enforcement receipt.
Data-residency guidance declares Enterprise Cloud and data-residency scope, not a generic GHES or personal-plan guarantee.
An eligible enterprise can enable a policy described as keeping inference processing and associated Copilot data in its designated region; actual behavior remains unverified.
The pinned supported-region list contains United States and European Union; it is not a current independent service-availability census.
Future region expansion is a plan, not released capability.

When residency enforcement is enabled, the source claims requests use regional model endpoints and code/prompts/responses stay in-region during inference processing; this is not observed traffic evidence.
Authentication tokens are described as granting only regional-endpoint access; no credential or routing test is supplied by documentation review.
The source claims only certified regional models are surfaced and models outside the region cannot be accessed under enforcement; this must be tested rather than inferred from list membership.
Copilot-related logs and telemetry are described as using region-appropriate compliant storage; this broader storage claim remains a source assertion, not verified retention/location.
Client compatibility, supported features and regional model-availability timing are shared dependencies of the residency procedure.
Some listed regional models may be utility-only; listed presence does not imply direct user model-picker selection.
The US region uses the shared US-model list, whose editorial note distinguishes current overlap from permanent equivalence with FedRAMP.
The shared compliance pricing reusable applies to residency enforcement as well as FedRAMP; it is not two cumulative surcharges by implication.
The Restrict Copilot to data residency compliant models policy is disabled by default and has pricing impact; it is a distinct control from FedRAMP restriction.
The linked enterprise policy procedure supplies navigation, not adopted policy, authorization or effective state.
The source describes the interface model selector as showing available regional models; interface visibility alone is not an enforcement behavior test.
Regional model availability changes over time and may lag public release while infrastructure and certification are obtained.
An editorial note says US-resident and FedRAMP-compliant model lists currently coincide but may diverge; residency must not be equated permanently with certification.
Model enforcement requires compatible client versions; the source gives a general 2025-or-later extension/CLI heuristic, not a complete exact-version compatibility matrix.
An incompatible older client is described as requiring an update before continuing; no client behavior test or observed block is supplied.
The source says all GA features work with enforcement and links policy visibility; this remains bounded by product eligibility and actual model/client compatibility.
The source promises compliant model alternatives for preview features at GA release; it does not establish present preview support.
Enforced requests are described as consuming 10% more AI credits due to regional/compliance endpoint infrastructure costs; pinned pricing is not a current invoice.
The source illustrates 100 credits becoming 110 and applies the pricing to compliant requests across all providers; it does not authorize costs or reveal utility-model billing interaction.
The billing reference remains separately unreviewed through this link, including thresholds, account budgets and pricing exceptions.
